tasks.title: Space Debris: A Growing Concern
paras: The Kessler Syndrome, proposed by NASA scientist Donald J.Kessler in 1978, hypothesizes a cascading effect in low Earth orbit (LEO) in which collisions between satellites and debris—defunct satellites, spent rocket stages, and fragments from earlier collisions—generate more fragments, exponentially increasing the likelihood of further collisions. This feedback loop could render certain orbital regions unusable for decades. While the model is compelling, some assumptions merit scrutiny. For instance, it presumes a uniform distribution of debris and constant collision probability, yet orbital mechanics suggest that debris clusters in specific altitudes and orbital paths, potentially limiting the scope of cascading events.

Moreover, technological advancements in debris tracking and active removal may mitigate the risk more effectively than Kessler originally envisioned. Critics argue that the syndrome underestimates the resilience of orbital infrastructure and overstates the inevitability of runaway collisions. Alternative explanations for observed debris growth include a greater number of satellite launches and fragmentation from aging spacecraft, rather than a self-sustaining cascade.

Nonetheless, the Kessler Syndrome remains a valuable heuristic for space policy, emphasizing the need for international cooperation and sustainable orbital practices. Its cautionary implications are profound—especially as commercial constellations dramatically increase the number of active satellites in LEO.

questions.stem: The passage suggests that one impact of the Kessler Syndrome would be

options.A: an increase in NASA space research
options.B: a limitation on where satellites could safely orbit
options.C: a greater number of satellite launches
options.D: an increased risk of debris falling to Earth

questions.analysis: 解析： 文中明确说明："This feedback loop could render certain orbital regions unusable for decades"（这种反馈循环可能使某些轨道区域数十年无法使用），即限制了卫星可以安全运行的轨道区域。 选项分析： A. NASA太空研究增加：未提及。 C. 更多卫星发射：这是碎片增长的替代解释，不是Kessler综合征的影响。 D. 碎片坠落地球风险增加：文中讨论的是轨道碰撞，不是坠落地球。

questions.stem: Why does the author mention the assertion that "debris clusters in specific altitudes and orbital paths"?

options.A: To provide a reason for an increase in collisions between satellites and debris
options.B: To illustrate a part of the feedback loop
options.C: To explain an objection to the Kessler Syndrome hypothesis
options.D: To emphasize the need for better debris tracking

questions.analysis: 解析： 文中先说"some assumptions merit scrutiny"（一些假设值得审视），然后举例：Kessler假设碎片均匀分布，但"orbital mechanics suggest that debris clusters in specific altitudes and orbital paths, potentially limiting the scope of cascading events"（碎片聚集在特定高度和轨道，可能限制级联事件的范围）。这是对Kessler假设的质疑/反对意见。 选项分析： A. 提供碰撞增加的原因：这是质疑Kessler假设的证据，不是支持碰撞增加。 B. 说明反馈循环的一部分：这是反对反馈循环无限扩大的观点。 D. 强调需要更好的碎片追踪：未提及。

questions.stem: The word "resilience" in the passage is closest in meaning to
questions.analysis: 解析： "underestimates the resilience of orbital infrastructure"意为"低估了轨道基础设施的恢复力/韧性"。resilience指承受压力后恢复原状的能力。 选项分析： A. strength（强度、韧性）：意思最接近。 B. threat（威胁）：相反含义。 C. knowledge（知识）：无关。 D. supervision（监督）：无关。

questions.stem: According to the passage, some argue that the Kessler Syndrome will not occur for all of the following reasons EXCEPT:

options.A: Space debris may not be spread out as evenly as the theory assumes.
options.B: New technology means that the removal of debris may be possible.
options.C: NASA has since developed new orbital infrastructure for avoiding collisions.
options.D: There may be other explanations for the observed growth in debris.

questions.analysis: 解析： 文中提到的反对Kessler综合征的理由： 选项分析： A. "debris clusters in specific altitudes" = 碎片分布不均匀（对应A） B. "technological advancements in debris tracking and active removal" = 新技术可清除碎片（对应B） C. NASA开发了新的轨道基础设施来避免碰撞：文中完全未提及，因此是EXCEPT选项。 D. "Alternative explanations for observed debris growth include..." = 有其他解释（对应D）

questions.stem: What does "Its cautionary implications" refer to in the passage?

options.A: The idea that one must assess the Kessler Syndrome carefully before accepting its predictions
options.B: The idea that there will be cascading collisions in LEO, making it difficult for satellites to remain intact
options.C: The suggestion that international cooperation will be more difficult to achieve as space becomes more cluttered
options.D: The suggestion that debris tracking and active removal may pose additional risks to satellites

questions.analysis: 解析： "Its cautionary implications"中的"It"指代Kessler Syndrome。该综合征的警示意义在于：如果不加控制，会发生级联碰撞，使轨道区域无法使用。这与前文描述的"collisions...generate more fragments, exponentially increasing the likelihood of further collisions"（碰撞产生更多碎片，指数级增加进一步碰撞的可能性）相呼应。 选项分析： A. 必须仔细评估Kessler综合征：这是对待理论的态度，不是理论本身的警示意义。 C. 国际合作将更难实现：文中说需要国际合作，不是说合作会更难。 D. 碎片追踪和清除可能带来额外风险：文中说这些技术可以mitigate（减轻）风险，不是增加风险。
